title: Stage 1: Meet the app
summary: The API you will containerize, what goes into its build context, and a .dockerignore that keeps junk out.

steps.title: What you are containerizing
body: Over this project you take **TodoApi**, a small ASP.NET Core minimal API, from "runs with `dotnet run` on my laptop" to a production-ready image running next to Postgres in Compose:
1. **this stage**: the app and its build context
2. a naive Dockerfile that works but is huge
4. Compose with Postgres, a volume and a healthcheck
Here is the real app. It reads its connection string from configuration, so the image never needs to know where the database lives:
await using var cmd = db.CreateCommand("select id, title, done from todos order by id");
await using var r = await cmd.ExecuteReaderAsync();
while (await r.ReadAsync()) list.Add(new Todo(r.GetInt32(0), r.GetString(1), r.GetBoolean(2)));
record Todo(int Id, string Title, bool Done);

steps.prompt: Why does the app read the connection string from configuration instead of hard-coding `Host=localhost`?
options: So one image can run anywhere: the environment (Compose, staging, production) supplies the right connection string
Because Npgsql cannot parse literal strings
Because containers cannot use localhost at all
steps.explain: Build once, configure per environment. In Compose it will be `ConnectionStrings__Default=Host=db;...`.

steps.prompt: Should each path be sent to the builder (build context) for the production image?
steps.explain: `.env` holds a local password; it must never be baked into an image. `bin/obj` are Windows/macOS build outputs that would clash with the Linux build.
`**/bin` matches a `bin` folder at any depth, including inside `tests/`.

steps.title: Which files reach the builder?
prompt: Write `List<string> Context(List<string> files, List<string> patterns)` that applies `.dockerignore` patterns to repository-relative paths (forward slashes). Supported patterns (a trailing `/` is ignored):
- `**/NAME` ignores any path with a segment equal to NAME (`**/bin` matches `bin/x.dll` and `tests/T/bin/y.dll`)
- `*.EXT` ignores top-level files ending in `.EXT` (`*.md` matches `README.md`, not `docs/a.md`)
- `NAME` ignores the path NAME and anything under `NAME/`
Patterns apply in order and the **last matching pattern wins**. Return the kept files in input order, followed by `N files sent, M ignored`.
template: Dojo.Eq("the project's .dockerignore", new List<string> { "Program.cs", "TodoApi.csproj", "appsettings.json", "docs/setup.md", "4 files sent, 6 ignored" }, Context(dojoFiles, new List<string> { "**/bin", "**/obj/", ".git", ".env", "*.md" }));

Dojo.Eq("re-include wins when last", new List<string> { "README.md", "Program.cs", "2 files sent, 1 ignored" }, Context(new List<string> { "README.md", "CHANGELOG.md", "Program.cs" }, new List<string> { "*.md", "!README.md" }));

Dojo.Eq("a later pattern can ignore again", new List<string> { "Program.cs", "1 files sent, 1 ignored" }, Context(new List<string> { "README.md", "Program.cs" }, new List<string> { "!README.md", "*.md" }));
hints: Write `bool Matches(string pattern, string file)` for the three forms, then loop over patterns keeping the last verdict.

steps.title: The same API, in the sandbox
steps.body: The sandbox has no Postgres or NuGet, so the next exercise is the same API with an in-memory list instead of Npgsql. Everything about how it is containerized stays the same.

steps.title: Write the API
prompt: Write the TodoApi `Program.cs` with an in-memory list. **Run checks** starts your server and calls it.
- `GET /todos` → `200`, a JSON array that starts with two todos: `{ "id": 1, "title": "Write a Dockerfile", "done": false }` and `{ "id": 2, "title": "Ship it", "done": false }`
- `POST /todos` with `{ "title": "..." }` → `201 Created`, the new todo with the next id (`3` for the first one created)
Put `record Todo(int Id, string Title, bool Done);` after `app.Run();`.
solution: var todos = new List<Todo> { new(1, "Write a Dockerfile", false), new(2, "Ship it", false) };
var created = new Todo(todos.Count + 1, input.Title, false);
record Todo(int Id, string Title, bool Done);
template: public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
Dojo.Check("GET /todos returns an array", list.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array, "expected a JSON array");
Dojo.Eq("GET /todos starts with two todos", 2, list.GetArrayLength());
if (list.GetArrayLength() > 0) Dojo.Eq("the first todo's title", "Write a Dockerfile", DojoWeb.Prop(list[0], "title"));
var post = await http.PostAsJsonAsync("/todos", new { title = "Add compose" });
Dojo.Eq("the new todo gets id 3", "3", DojoWeb.Prop(created, "id"));
Dojo.Eq("the new todo is not done", "false", DojoWeb.Prop(created, "done"));
Dojo.Eq("GET /todos now has three", 3, after.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array ? after.GetArrayLength() : 0);
hints: `app.MapGet("/todos", () => todos);` serialises the list as JSON.
